trace.title: Observed symptom
trace.detail:
# The idea

Debug from an observed symptom. Write the exact steps, expected result, and actual result.

Decide which boundary could explain the difference: URL, state ownership, request ordering, server response, cache, rendering identity, or browser layout.

Unit tests suit pure transformations. Component tests suit interaction and visible states.

A small end-to-end test checks that important boundaries connect. Avoid replacing every dependency with a mock and calling the result a full application test.

Capstone: a searchable task list with a URL filter, editable title, save failure recovery, stable row identity, and stale-response protection.

Use either React or Vue for the implementation, then explain the same state ownership in the other framework. Next.js is an optional boundary exercise, not a reason to rebuild every screen.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
Reproduce with the smallest synthetic dataset. Follow the event through handler, state update, request, accepted response, and render.

Add one regression test at the boundary that failed.

For completion, demonstrate direct-link refresh, back navigation, one failed save without data loss, one out-of-order request, keyboard use, and a mobile layout. Explain what your tests cover and what they do not.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: A snapshot test alone may not reveal that an old request overwrites a new result. A component test in a simulated DOM also cannot prove all real browser layout or accessibility behavior.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Prove one task-editing flow across state, requests, rendering, and accessibility. Give a concrete failure example.
